headline: Indian stock markets face selling pressure following RBI rate hike and hawkish global cues

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: RBI hiked interest rates for the first time in nearly four years, triggering market selling.
US Fed minutes signaled another rate hike by year-end as inflation remains high.
Rising US Treasury yields caused foreign investors to pull out $26.3 billion from emerging markets in September.
Major heavyweights like Hindalco, Adani Enterprises, and Infosys faced notable decline.
whatHappening: Sensex dropped 429 points while Nifty settled around 22,600 after the RBI rate announcement.
Hindalco declined by 3% and Infosys fell 2%, leading market losses.
RBI report noted that India's rural economy is increasingly decoupling from monsoon shocks.
US markets closed lower off record highs as Treasury yields continued to climb.
summary:
Indian benchmark indices closed sharply lower after the RBI increased interest rates for the first time in nearly four years.
Global markets added pressure as hawkish Fed signals and rising US Treasury yields accelerated foreign capital outflows from emerging markets.
Heavyweights including Hindalco, Infosys, and Adani Enterprises dragged the indices down amidst cautious investor sentiment.
